questionText: Under the "PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana" approved by the Union Cabinet in February 2024, how many units of free electricity per month are targeted for 1 crore households via rooftop solar installations?
explanation: With an outlay of Rs 75,021 crore, PM-Surya Ghar provides up to 300 units of free electricity monthly to one crore households with central subsidies up to 60% for solar rooftop plants.

questionText: Who took oath as the 50th Chief Justice of India (CJI) in November 2022?
explanation: Justice Dhananjaya Yeshwant Chandrachud was sworn in as the 50th Chief Justice of India on November 9, 2022, serving a two-year tenure until November 10, 2024.

questionText: Who was sworn in as the 51st Chief Justice of India on November 11, 2024?
explanation: Justice Sanjiv Khanna was administered the oath of office as the 51st Chief Justice of India by President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan on November 11, 2024.

questionText: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023) reserves what proportion of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies?
explanation: Passed during the special session in the new Parliament building in September 2023, the 106th Amendment reserves 33% of seats in Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, and Delhi Assembly for women for a period of 15 years.

questionText: The three new criminal laws replacing the IPC, CrPC, and Indian Evidence Act across India came into legal effect on:
explanation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) came into force nationwide on July 1, 2024.

questionText: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023, which colonial-era provision was formally repealed and replaced with offenses against the sovereignty and integrity of India?
explanation: The archaic offense of "Sedition" under Section 124A of the IPC was repealed and replaced with Section 152 in BNS penalizing acts endangering sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.

questionText: The "Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan" (PM-JANMAN) launched from Khunti, Jharkhand, in November 2023 is focused on:
options: Comprehensive socio-economic saturation of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)
Free air travel for tribal pilgrims
explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched PM-JANMAN on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas from Khunti, Jharkhand, with a budget of Rs 24,000 crore to provide housing, clean water, electricity, and roads to 75 PVTG communities across India.

questionText: November 15, the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, was declared by the Government of India in 2021 as:
explanation: The Union Cabinet declared November 15 as "Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas" to honor the invaluable role of tribal freedom fighters in India’s independence struggle.

questionText: The High-Level Committee on "One Nation, One Election" submitted its recommendations in March 2024 under the chairmanship of:
options: Ram Nath Kovind (Former President of India)
explanation: The committee chaired by former President Ram Nath Kovind submitted its report on March 14, 2024, recommending simultaneous elections for Lok Sabha and State Assemblies followed by local body elections within 100 days.

questionText: India’s first underwater metro service, passing through a 520-meter tunnel beneath the Hooghly River, was inaugurated in March 2024 in which city?
explanation: Part of Kolkata Metro’s Green Line, this engineering feat traverses beneath the Hooghly River in 45 seconds, connecting Kolkata and Howrah at a depth of 32 meters below water level.

questionText: The "Atal Setu" (Mumbai Trans Harbour Link - MTHL), inaugurated in January 2024, holds what distinction in Indian infrastructure?
options: Longest sea bridge in India (21.8 km)
explanation: Atal Bihari Vajpayee Sewri-Nhava Sheva Atal Setu is a 21.8 km 6-lane sea bridge (16.5 km over sea) connecting Sewri in Mumbai to Chirle in Navi Mumbai.

questionText: Who was appointed the Election Commissioner of India in March 2024 alongside Rajiv Kumar as CEC?
options: Gyanesh Kumar and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu
Arun Goel and Anup Chandra Pandey
Sunil Arora and Achal Kumar Joti
explanation: Former bureaucrats Gyanesh Kumar and Dr. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu were appointed as Election Commissioners in March 2024 under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners Act, 2023.

questionText: Which state in February 2024 became the first in independent India to pass and enact a "Uniform Civil Code" (UCC) Bill?
explanation: The Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly passed the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill on February 7, 2024, providing common rules for marriage, divorce, inheritance, and live-in relationships (Goa’s UCC predates independence).

questionText: The Supreme Court of India in February 2024 unanimously struck down which controversial political funding instrument as unconstitutional and violative of Article 19(1)(a)?
explanation: A 5-judge Constitution Bench headed by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud held that anonymous Electoral Bonds violate citizens' right to information about political funding sources.

questionText: Who was awarded the prestigious Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024 for his lifelong championship of farmers' rights and rural development?
explanation: Former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh was honored posthumously with India’s highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in February 2024.

questionText: Former Bihar Chief Minister Karpoori Thakur, revered as "Jan Nayak" for pioneering reservation policies for backward classes, was conferred which award posthumously in 2024?
explanation: Karpoori Thakur was conferred the Bharat Ratna on January 23, 2024, in his centenary birth year, honoring his steadfast commitment to the marginalized.

questionText: Veteran statesman Lal Krishna Advani was conferred the Bharat Ratna in 2024. Which high constitutional office did he occupy from 2002 to 2004?
explanation: L. K. Advani served as the 7th Deputy Prime Minister of India in the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government, awarded the Bharat Ratna in February 2024.

questionText: The "Lakhpati Didi" initiative launched by the Government of India aims to empower self-help group (SHG) rural women to achieve:
options: A sustainable household income of at least Rs 1 lakh per annum
Free bank credit up to Rs 1 lakh
One lakh rupees in insurance payouts
explanation: The Lakhpati Didi scheme, with an enhanced target of 3 crore women under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-NRLM, trains women SHG members in LED making, plumbing, drone piloting, and organic farming.

questionText: The "Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana" (PMMSY) is implemented to accelerate the sustainable development of:
explanation: PMMSY was launched in September 2020 with an investment of Rs 20,050 crore to drive the "Blue Revolution" through modern harbors, cold chains, and seaweed culture.

questionText: The "Vibrant Villages Programme" (VVP) approved by the Union Cabinet in 2023 focuses on comprehensive infrastructure and livelihood development of:
options: Border villages located along India’s northern border with China
Coastal fishing hamlets along Arabian Sea
explanation: VVP covers 2,967 border villages across Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Ladakh to strengthen border security and reverse outward migration.

questionText: What is the vision document titled "Viksit Bharat @ 2047" launched by the Government of India?
options: A national strategic roadmap to transform India into a fully developed nation by the centenary of its independence in 2047
An environmental plan to eliminate coal power by 2047
A digital mission to automate governance
explanation: Viksit Bharat @ 2047 sets multi-sectoral targets to expand India’s economy to $30 trillion, achieve high human development indices, and achieve technological self-reliance by 2047.

questionText: In May 2023, the historic golden sceptre "Sengol", symbolizing righteous governance from the Chola dynasty, was installed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in:
options: The new Parliament House, near the Speaker’s chair in the Lok Sabha
explanation: The historic Sengol, originally presented to Jawaharlal Nehru on the eve of independence in 1947 by the Thiruvavaduthurai Adheenam, was formally installed beside the Speaker’s chair in the new Lok Sabha chamber.

questionText: The "Amrit Bharat Station Scheme" launched by Indian Railways in 2023 envisages:
options: The modernization and redevelopment of 1,300+ railway stations across India with modern passenger amenities and roof plazas
explanation: The scheme masterplans the phased upgrading of over 1,300 stations into modern city centers with waiting lounges, free Wi-Fi, multi-modal integration, and heritage aesthetics.

questionText: Which Indian port city in Gujarat became the terminal base for the historic India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) announced at the G20 Summit?
explanation: IMEC connects ports on India's western seaboard (Kandla, Mundra, JNPT) across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Israel to European ports (Piraeus).

questionText: Who was appointed the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women (NCW) in October 2024?
explanation: Vijaya Rahatkar, former chief of the Maharashtra State Commission for Women, assumed charge as the 9th Chairperson of the National Commission for Women in October 2024.

questionText: In the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2023 announced in January 2024, which two cities shared the joint title of the "Cleanest City of India"?
explanation: Indore bagged the cleanest city award for an unprecedented 7th consecutive time, sharing the top rank jointly with Surat in the category of cities with a population over 1 lakh.

questionText: Which state in India was ranked the "Cleanest State" in the Swachh Survekshan 2023?
explanation: Maharashtra secured the first position among cleanest states in the country, followed by Madhya Pradesh in second place and Chhattisgarh in third.

questionText: The "Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0" (PMAY-U 2.0) approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2024 targets constructing how many houses for urban poor and middle-class families over 5 years?
options: 1 crore houses with an investment of Rs 10 lakh crore
explanation: PMAY-U 2.0 provides financial assistance to construct 1 crore affordable houses for EWS, LIG, and Middle-Income Group families in urban areas.

questionText: Which national mission was launched with an outlay of Rs 10,372 crore in March 2024 to democratize artificial intelligence computing capacity in India?
explanation: The IndiaAI Mission establishes high-end computing infrastructure (over 10,000 GPUs) through public-private partnerships, the IndiaAI Innovation Centre, and foundation model development.

questionText: The "Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana" (PM-MKSSY) approved in February 2024 is designed as a sub-scheme under PMMSY to:
options: Formalize the unorganized fisheries sector and provide institutional credit and insurance access to fishers
explanation: With an investment of over Rs 6,000 crore, PM-MKSSY facilitates digital registration of fishers on the National Fisheries Digital Platform and supports micro-enterprises.

questionText: In which state was the Sela Tunnel, the world’s longest twin-lane bi-directional tunnel at an altitude above 13,000 feet, dedicated to the nation by PM Modi in March 2024?
explanation: Constructed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) at 13,700 ft, the 1.5 km Sela Tunnel provides all-weather military and civilian connectivity to Tawang near the LAC.

questionText: What is "Bhashini" developed by the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY)?
options: An AI-powered National Public Digital Platform for local language machine translation across Indian languages
A digital library for ancient manuscripts
A speech therapy app for hospitals
explanation: Bhashini leverages natural language processing and voice recognition to enable digital services and translations across all 22 scheduled Indian languages in real time.

questionText: India’s first commercial semiconductor fabrication facility (Fab) was approved in February 2024 to be set up at Dholera (Gujarat) by Tata Electronics in partnership with:
explanation: Tata Electronics partnered with Taiwan’s PSMC to construct the Rs 91,000-crore semiconductor plant at Dholera Special Investment Region with an initial capacity of 50,000 wafers per month.

questionText: Which city hosted the 27th National Youth Festival in January 2024, inaugurated on the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda?
explanation: The 27th National Youth Festival was organized from January 12 to 16, 2024, at Nashik under the theme "MY Bharat-Viksit Bharat@2047: By the youth, For the youth".

questionText: Who was appointed the President of the 78th Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)?
explanation: Dennis Francis, veteran diplomat from Trinidad and Tobago, served as the President of the 78th session of the UNGA, visiting India on an official mission in January 2024.

questionText: During India’s G20 Presidency in September 2023 at the New Delhi Summit, which regional organization was admitted as a permanent 21st member of the G20?
explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi invited Azali Assoumani, Chairperson of the 55-nation African Union, to assume its seat as a permanent member of the newly enlarged G21.

questionText: What was the official theme of India’s G20 Presidency in 2023?
options: "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" — "One Earth, One Family, One Future"
explanation: Drawn from the Maha Upanishad, the Sanskrit motto "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" (One Earth, One Family, One Future) encapsulated India's inclusive, action-oriented G20 agenda.

questionText: Which country hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in November 2024, continuing the Global South troika from India?
explanation: Brazil held the 2024 G20 Presidency under President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, hosting the summit at the Museum of Modern Art in Rio de Janeiro in November 2024.

questionText: Which five countries officially joined the BRICS grouping as new full members on January 1, 2024?
options: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE)
Argentina, Nigeria, Indonesia, Turkey, and Mexico
Algeria, Kazakhstan, Vietnam, Cuba, and Belarus
Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Bhutan
explanation: Following the 15th BRICS Summit in Johannesburg, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and UAE joined Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa as full members.

questionText: Which country hosted the 16th BRICS Summit in October 2024 in the city of Kazan?
explanation: The 16th BRICS Summit was held in Kazan, Russia, from October 22 to 24, 2024, under the motto "Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security".

questionText: The historic UN Climate Change Conference COP28 in December 2023, which concluded with the "UAE Consensus" calling for transitioning away from fossil fuels, was held in:
explanation: COP28 in Dubai presided by Sultan Al Jaber operationalized the Loss and Damage Fund and explicitly pledged to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems.

questionText: Which country hosted the COP29 UN Climate Summit in November 2024?
explanation: The 2024 UN Climate Conference (COP29) took place in Baku, Azerbaijan, focusing predominantly on climate finance negotiations (the New Collective Quantified Goal - NCQG).

questionText: In March 2024, Sweden officially became the 32nd member state of which military alliance?
explanation: Following Finland’s accession in 2023 as the 31st member, Sweden deposited its instrument of accession in Washington on March 7, 2024, ending two centuries of military non-alignment.

questionText: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, is seated in which city?
explanation: Established in 1945, the ICJ comprises 15 judges elected by the UN General Assembly and Security Council, headquartered at the Peace Palace in The Hague.

questionText: Who was elected as the President of the World Bank Group in June 2023?
explanation: Indian-born American business executive Ajay Banga took office as the 14th President of the World Bank on June 2, 2023, becoming the first Indian-American to lead the institution.

questionText: Who serves as the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), reappointed for a second 5-year term starting October 2024?
explanation: Bulgarian economist Kristalina Georgieva was selected for a second five-year term as IMF Managing Director, while Indian-American economist Gita Gopinath serves as First Deputy Managing Director.

questionText: Who was appointed the Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO), re-elected in 2022 for a second term?
explanation: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus of Ethiopia has served as Director-General of WHO since 2017, steering the global health response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

questionText: Which multilateral initiative was launched at COP28 by India and the UAE to incentivize voluntary planet-positive actions by individuals and communities?
explanation: PM Narendra Modi co-hosted the launch of the Global Green Credit Initiative alongside President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan to reward eco-friendly afforestation and water conservation.

questionText: The Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA) was formally unveiled in September 2023 on the sidelines of the G20 Summit by India together with which co-founding countries?
explanation: The GBA was launched by PM Modi with US President Joe Biden and Brazilian President Lula da Silva to establish global standards for biofuels and accelerate trade in sustainable ethanol.

questionText: Which country won the presidency of the 2024 50th G7 Summit held in June 2024 at Borgo Egnazia, Apulia?
explanation: Italy held the G7 Presidency in 2024, hosting leaders of the Group of Seven and outreach partners including PM Narendra Modi in the scenic Puglia region.

questionText: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit was hosted in July 2024 in which city?
explanation: Kazakhstan hosted the 24th Meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State in Astana in July 2024, where Belarus was formally admitted as the 10th full member state.

questionText: Which country in July 2024 was officially inducted as the 10th permanent member state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
explanation: Following Iran’s entry in 2023, Belarus completed all legal accession procedures at the Astana Summit in July 2024 to become the 10th full member of the SCO.

questionText: The Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad) comprises which four democratic maritime nations?
options: India, United States, Japan, and Australia
USA, UK, Australia, and New Zealand
India, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore
explanation: The Quad is a strategic diplomatic partnership committed to supporting an open, stable, inclusive, and rules-based Indo-Pacific free from coercion.

questionText: Which international economic grouping is commonly referred to as "I2U2"?
options: India, Israel, United Arab Emirates, and United States
explanation: I2U2 is a minilateral economic partnership focusing on joint investments in water, energy, transportation, space, health, and food security across the Middle East and South Asia.

questionText: What is the "International Solar Alliance" (ISA) co-founded by India and France in 2015, whose permanent secretariat is located at:
explanation: The ISA, launched by PM Narendra Modi and French President Francois Hollande at COP21, is headquartered at the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE) campus in Gurugram, India.

questionText: Which country in March 2024 signed a historic $100 billion Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) with India?
options: European Free Trade Association (EFTA - Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein)
explanation: India signed the landmark TEPA with the 4-nation EFTA bloc on March 10, 2024, under which EFTA will invest $100 billion in India over 15 years, generating 1 million direct jobs.

questionText: Which country topped the United Nations World Happiness Report in 2024 for the seventh consecutive year?
explanation: Finland secured the number one rank in the World Happiness Report 2024 published by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network, followed by Denmark and Iceland.

questionText: What was India’s rank in the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2024 published by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)?
explanation: India rose to 39th rank out of 133 economies in the Global Innovation Index 2024, maintaining its leadership as the top innovation economy in Central and Southern Asia.

questionText: What was India’s rank in the UNDP Human Development Index (HDI) report for 2023–24 (with an HDI score of 0.644)?
explanation: In the 2023/24 Human Development Report "Breaking the Gridlock", India ranked 134th out of 193 nations, placed in the Medium Human Development category.

questionText: The headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is situated in:
explanation: Founded in 1957 as the world’s "Atoms for Peace" organization within the UN system, the IAEA is headquartered at the Vienna International Centre in Austria.

questionText: Which strategic choke point waterway connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman carries approximately one-fifth of global petroleum consumption?
explanation: The Strait of Hormuz, lying between Oman and Iran, is the world's most critical oil transit chokepoint through which over 20 million barrels of crude oil pass daily.

questionText: The Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, frequently in global news due to maritime disruptions by Houthi rebels in 2023–2024, connects:
options: Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden (Arabian Sea)
explanation: Bab-el-Mandeb (Gate of Tears) connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden between Djibouti and Yemen, serving as the southern maritime access gate to the Suez Canal.

questionText: Which island territory was confirmed as the venue for the 2024 G20 Summit by South Africa for 2025?
options: South Africa will host the G20 in 2025 across Johannesburg
explanation: South Africa assumed the G20 Presidency on December 1, 2024, culminating in the 2025 Leaders' Summit, marking the first time an African nation presides over the G20.

questionText: Who was sworn in as the 47th President of the United States following the November 2024 presidential election?
explanation: Republican candidate Donald Trump won the November 5, 2024, presidential election, securing a non-consecutive second term as the 47th President of the United States.

questionText: Which country officially launched the "Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty" at the Rio G20 Summit in November 2024?
explanation: Brazilian President Lula da Silva launched the Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty with over 140 founding members (including India) to eradicate hunger through targeted conditional cash transfers.

questionText: At the 33rd Summer Olympic Games held in Paris in July-August 2024, how many total medals did the Indian contingent secure?
explanation: India won 6 medals at Paris 2024: Neeraj Chopra (Silver in javelin), Manu Bhaker (2 Bronze in shooting), Sarabjot Singh (Bronze in mixed shooting), Swapnil Kusale (Bronze in shooting), and the Men’s Hockey team (Bronze).

questionText: Who made history at the Paris 2024 Olympics as the first athlete in independent India to win two Olympic medals at a single edition of the Olympic Games?
explanation: Manu Bhaker won bronze in the Women’s 10m Air Pistol and a second bronze alongside Sarabjot Singh in the 10m Air Pistol Mixed Team event at Paris 2024.

questionText: Neeraj Chopra won the Silver Medal in Men’s Javelin Throw at the Paris 2024 Olympics with a best throw of 89.45 meters. Who won the Gold Medal with an Olympic record throw of 92.97 meters?
explanation: Arshad Nadeem of Pakistan set a new Olympic record with a 92.97m throw to capture gold, while defending Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra claimed silver.

questionText: Which country won the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2024 held in the United States and the West Indies in June 2024?
options: India (defeated South Africa in the final)
explanation: India, captained by Rohit Sharma, defeated South Africa by 7 runs at Bridgetown, Barbados, on June 29, 2024, winning its second ICC Men’s T20 World Cup title undefeated.

questionText: At the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games, India achieved its best-ever performance in Paralympic history by winning how many total medals?
explanation: India shattered all past records at the Paris Paralympics, finishing 18th in the overall medal table with 29 medals, anchored by gold medalists like Avani Lekhara, Sumit Antil, and Harvinder Singh.

questionText: Who became the first Indian woman archer to win an individual Paralympic Gold Medal at Paris 2024 with her armless shooting style?
options: Sheetal Devi (won bronze in mixed team with Rakesh Kumar)
explanation: 17-year-old armless sensation Sheetal Devi from Jammu & Kashmir shot bullseyes with her feet, winning bronze in mixed compound archery alongside Rakesh Kumar.

questionText: Who won the 58th Jnanpith Award announced in February 2024?
explanation: The Jnanpith Selection Board conferred the 58th Jnanpith Award jointly on renowned poet-lyricist Gulzar for Urdu and spiritual polymath Jagadguru Rambhadracharya for Sanskrit.

questionText: Who was conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, India’s highest award in cinema, for the year 2022 (announced in 2024)?
explanation: Legendary actor Mithun Chakraborty was honored with the Dadasaheb Phalke Lifetime Achievement Award at the 70th National Film Awards ceremony in New Delhi.

questionText: At the 70th National Film Awards announced in August 2024, which film won the National Award for Best Feature Film?
explanation: The Malayalam suspense chamber-drama film Aattam, directed by Anand Ekarshi, won the prestigious Golden Lotus (Swarna Kamal) for Best Feature Film.

questionText: Who won the Best Actor award at the 70th National Film Awards for 2022?
explanation: Rishab Shetty was adjudged Best Actor for his performance as Shiva in the Kannada folk-action masterpiece Kantara.

questionText: Who won the 2024 Booker Prize for her climate fiction novel "Orbital"?
explanation: British author Samantha Harvey won the 2024 Booker Prize for "Orbital", a contemplative novel chronicling a single day in the lives of six astronauts aboard the International Space Station.

questionText: Who won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Literature "for her intense poetic prose that confronts historical traumas and exposes the fragility of human life"?
explanation: Han Kang became the first South Korean author and first Asian female writer to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature, acclaimed for works like "The Vegetarian" and "Human Acts".

questionText: The 2024 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to which Japanese grassroots organization of atomic bomb survivors from Hiroshima and Nagasaki?
explanation: Nihon Hidankyo was awarded the 2024 Nobel Peace Prize for its tireless efforts to achieve a world free of nuclear weapons and demonstrating that nuclear weapons must never be used again.

questionText: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable:
options: Machine learning with artificial neural networks
explanation: American physicist John Hopfield and British-Canadian scientist Geoffrey Hinton (hailed as the Godfather of AI) received the Physics Nobel for using physics principles to pioneer artificial neural networks.

questionText: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to David Baker (computational protein design) and Demis Hassabis & John Jumper (Google DeepMind) for:
options: Protein structure prediction using artificial intelligence (AlphaFold)
explanation: Demis Hassabis and John M. Jumper developed AlphaFold2, an AI model that predicted the 3D structures of virtually all 200 million known proteins, revolutionizing molecular biology.

questionText: The 2024 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson, and James A. Robinson for their research on:
options: How institutions are formed and affect prosperity (inclusive versus extractive political and economic institutions)
explanation: Acemoglu, Johnson, and Robinson (authors of "Why Nations Fail") demonstrated that societal institutions introduced during colonization explain why some nations prosper while others remain poor.

questionText: Which space science mission was launched by ISRO on January 1, 2024, to investigate the polarization of cosmic X-rays from black holes and neutron stars?
explanation: Launched aboard PSLV-C58, XPoSat is India’s first dedicated polarimetry mission and only the world’s second (after NASA’s IXPE) to study celestial X-ray sources.

questionText: What is the name of the humanoid female robot developed by ISRO for unmanned test flights ahead of the human Gaganyaan mission?
explanation: Vyommitra ("space friend") is designed with sensors to monitor environmental cabin parameters, operate switch panels, and simulate human physiology during Gaganyaan orbital trials.

questionText: Which DRDO-developed Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) technology flight was successfully flight-tested on March 11, 2024, under "Mission Divyastra"?
explanation: Mission Divyastra marked the inaugural flight test of the indigenously developed Agni-5 missile equipped with MIRV warheads capable of striking separate designated targets up to 5,000+ km.

questionText: Which Indian chess grandmaster won the FIDE Candidates Tournament in Toronto in April 2024 at age 17, becoming the youngest challenger in World Chess Championship history?
explanation: D. Gukesh scored 9/14 in Toronto to surpass Garry Kasparov’s 40-year-old record as the youngest ever challenger for the undisputed World Chess Championship title.

questionText: At the 45th FIDE Chess Olympiad held in Budapest in September 2024, what historic achievement did the Indian contingent attain?
options: Historic double gold medals in both Men’s (Open) and Women’s team sections
Silver in Open and Bronze in Women’s
explanation: India authored history by winning gold medals in both the Open (Gukesh, Praggnanandhaa, Arjun, Vidit, Harikrishna) and Women's (Harika, Vaishali, Divya, Vantika, Tania) sections at Budapest.

questionText: Which supersonic cruise missile manufactured through an Indo-Russian joint venture was officially delivered to the Armed Forces of the Philippines in April 2024 under a $375 million export contract?
explanation: India dispatched the first shore-based anti-ship battery of the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile to the Philippines Marines aboard an Indian Air Force C-17 Globemaster.

questionText: The bilateral joint military exercise "SADA TANSEEQ" was held for the first time in Rajasthan in January-February 2024 between the armies of India and:
explanation: Exercise SADA TANSEEQ was the inaugural joint military exercise between the Indian Army and the Royal Saudi Land Forces at the Mahajan Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan.

questionText: Exercise "CYCLONE-I" and "CYCLONE-II" are joint special forces exercises conducted between the armies of India and:
explanation: Exercise Cyclone was inaugurated in 2023 in Rajasthan and conducted in Anshas, Egypt, in 2024 to enhance tactical interoperability in desert counter-terrorism operations.

questionText: Who was awarded the prestigious Abel Prize 2024 by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters for groundbreaking contributions to probability theory and mathematical physics?
explanation: French mathematician Michel Talagrand received the 2024 Abel Prize (often called the Nobel of Mathematics) for his seminal work in Gaussian processes and concentration of measure.
